name: Cyprus
summary: Independent from Britain in 1960; divided since the Turkish invasion of 1974, with a Turkish Cypriot administration in the north recognised only by Turkey.

knownFor.label: Green Line
knownFor.note: UN buffer zone dividing the island.

location.value: The third-largest Mediterranean island, south of Turkey and west of Syria and Lebanon; about 9,250 km².

terrain.value: The Troodos mountains in the south-west, the Kyrenia range in the north and the Mesaoria plain between them.

climate.value: Hot, dry summers and mild winters; water shortages are common.

resources.value: Copper (which gave the island its name in antiquity), farmland, and gas fields found offshore since 2011.

population.value: About 930,000 in the Republic-controlled south and about 380,000 in the north.

urbanisation.value: Nicosia, the divided capital, plus Limassol, Larnaca and Paphos on the south coast.

disease.value: Good health care; a national health system (GESY) since 2019.

migration.value: About 160,000 Greek Cypriots and 50,000 Turkish Cypriots were displaced in 1974; settlers from Turkey moved to the north.

economicBase.value: Tourism, shipping (one of the largest merchant fleets in the EU), banking and services.

tradeRoutes.value: Between Europe and the Middle East; EU member since 2004.

wealth.value: A high-income economy in the south; the north depends on Turkey.

moneyAndTax.value: The Cypriot pound until the euro (2008); a banking crisis forced a bailout and a levy on large deposits (2013).

inequality.value: Moderate inequality; a large gap between the south and the north.

governmentType.value: A presidential republic: the president is both head of state and head of government.

succession.value: Presidential and parliamentary elections in the south; the north holds its own elections.

institutions.value: House of Representatives; the 1960 constitution’s power-sharing broke down in 1963–64.

stability.value: Intercommunal violence (1963–64); coup and Turkish invasion (1974).

eliteConflict.value: Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot leaders disagree on how to reunite the island.

armyAndTech.value: National Guard; Britain keeps two sovereign military bases (Akrotiri and Dhekelia).

majorWars.value: Intercommunal violence (1963–64); a Greek-backed coup and the Turkish invasion (1974).

territoryChange.value: The north is under a Turkish Cypriot administration recognised only by Turkey.

alliancesRivals.value: EU member but not in NATO; disputes with Turkey over the north and offshore gas.

scienceEducation.value: University of Cyprus (1989) and many private universities.

openness.value: An open economy and a hub for shipping companies.

communicationTransport.value: Roads and airports at Larnaca and Paphos; crossing points open between north and south since 2003.

religion.value: Greek Orthodox (Church of Cyprus) in the south; Sunni Muslim in the north.

languageWriting.value: Greek and Turkish are both official.

artsArchitecture.value: Painted Byzantine churches of Troodos, Roman mosaics at Paphos, Gothic and Venetian buildings.

socialStructure.value: Greek Cypriots (about 78%), Turkish Cypriots, and small Armenian and Maronite communities.

sharedIdentity.value: Greek Cypriot and Turkish Cypriot identities are divided; some people stress a shared Cypriot identity.

dailyLife.value: Houses and flats; halloumi cheese, meze, souvlaki and strong coffee.

neighbours.value: Turkey, Syria, Lebanon, Israel, Egypt, Greece.

ideasReligions.value: Orthodox Christianity and Islam side by side.

riseSignals.value: Independence (1960) after the EOKA campaign against British rule (1955–59).

declineSignals.value: Division of the island (1974) and the banking crisis (2013).

outcome.value: Still divided: the Republic of Cyprus and the self-declared Turkish Republic of Northern Cyprus (recognised only by Turkey).

overallCertainty.value: The status of the north is disputed.
